text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- British Sugar (BSO) has offered to buy a 38 percent stake in the Poland's biggest sugar mill, Ropczyce in the south east. Investors from Germany, Canada and Poland also presented bids.

- Polconsult experts approved plans to transform the Lask military airfield in central Poland into a passenger and cargo airport. The airport will be located next to the planned Warsaw-Wroclaw A-8 motorway.

- The Stollwerck Poland confectionery maker, which operates a chocolate plant in Jankowice, western Poland, has a 22.3 percent share in the chocolate market. Nestle Poland and its Goplana subsidiary together hold 19.8 percent market share, followed by Pepsico's Wedel with 19.4 percent, a report by the Nielsen monitoring firm said.

- Annual net profits of Poland's refineries in 1996 were 50 percent lower than the 1995 results due to excessive oil prices in the second half of the year, which ranged well above the initially forecast levels, the refineries said.
NOWA EUROPA

- Car owners will receive price discounts when buying Fiat cars if they scrap their old cars, the company said. Fiat is Poland's first automaker to promote environment protection through product pricing.

- Up to five billion zlotys worth of shares will enter Poland's capital market in 1997, mainly through privatisation of the KGHM copper combine and Bank Handlowy, and this can easily absorbed by the market, the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) president Jacek Socha said.

- Britain's National Express Group has decided to close down the Polski Express coach transport company, which brought a net loss of $750,000 in 1996. The loss was caused by the government subsidies to the national rail and coach services, Polski Express director Chris Watts said.
- The listed Animex food processor and trader has guaranteed a three million zlotys credit drawn by the Suwalki-based Suwalskie Zaklady Drobiarskie, Animex said.
- Credit Suisse Asset Management currently holds a 6.6 percent stake in the listed ComputerLand computer system integrator.
- The Krakow-based Mostostal Krakow construction firm has acquired 60 B-series certificates of deposit issued by the Bank Handlowy bank, nominally worth 100,000 zlotys each.
- The listed Jelfa pharmaceutical firm has issued three month papers nominally worth 5.3 million zlotys.

- Germany's Commerzbank is considering increasing its stake in the listed Bank Rozwoju Exportu (BRE) export development bank and acquiring a stake in BRE's new share issue at the end of 1996, BRE board member Janusz Maciejewicz said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- A new subsection of the Katowice Special Economic Zone in the Tychy area, southern Poland, was opened yesterday. Over 30 firms have already expressed interest in investing in the area, Tychy sub-zone president Ewa Stachura Pordzik said.
ZYCIE
- The Wroclaw-based Bank Zachodni bank together with the Forum Financial Group will form an open trust fund. The new fund's capital amounts to four million zlotys, the bank said.

- The Radom provincial prosecutor has accused three former directors of the state-owned BGZ agricultural sector bank of breaking financial law, which led to a loss of 20 million zlotys. The former bank directors deny the accusations.
PARKIET
- Coca Cola Poland has contracted the listed Exbud construction firm to carry out works for the Niepolomice bottling plant worth $1.3 million, Exbud said. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
